aztec_chalchiuhtotolin.value: chalchihuitl, jade or precious greenstone, plus totolin, turkey: 'jade turkey', or 'precious fowl'.

aztec_itzpapalotl.value: itztli, obsidian, plus papalotl, butterfly: 'obsidian butterfly', or 'clawed butterfly' on another reading of the first element.

aztec_patecatl.value: Lord of the Root of Pulque
From pahtli, medicine or drug, with the gentilic -tecatl: 'he of the medicines', 'the man from the land of medicines'.

aztec_quetzalcoatl.evidence: Pinturas1 versus8: distinct narrative contexts, no identity or genealogy transfer.

aztec_tepeyollotl.value: tepetl, mountain, plus yollotl, heart: 'heart of the mountain' — the jaguar in the cave, and the echo, which the Mexica understood as the mountain's own voice.

aztec_tepoztecatl.value: 'He of Tepoztlan', the town in the Tlahuica country whose god he is. His calendar name is Ometochtli, 'Two Rabbit'.

aztec_tlahuizcalpantecuhtli.value: 'Lord of the house of the dawn' — tlahuizcalli is the dawn light, -pan is 'in', tecuhtli is 'lord'. It is one of the longest theonyms in Nahuatl.

aztec_tonacacihuatl.value: 'Lady of our flesh' — the feminine of her husband's name. Under her other name, Omecihuatl, 'Two-Lady'.

aztec_tonacatecuhtli.value: 'Lord of our flesh' or 'lord of our sustenance' — tonacayotl is both the body and the food that makes it, which is the same thought twice. Under his other name, Ometecuhtli, 'Two-Lord'.

aztec_xolotl.value: The word means a servant or a page, and also a twin or a monstrous double; xoloitzcuintli, the hairless dog, is named from it.

purepecha_tiripeme_caheri.value: Tarascan; 'Caheri' means 'great/big' (cf. Curita-caheri, 'the great burning'), here distinguishing 'the great Tiripeme' installed at Pareo; given in the Relación in the Spanish orthography Caheri.

purepecha_tiripeme_quarencha.value: Tarascan; Tirípeme is the shared name of the brother direction-gods (Tiripemencha). 'Quarencha' distinguishes this eastern member; given in the Relación in the Spanish orthography Quarencha.

purepecha_tiripeme_turupten.value: Tarascan; 'Turupten' distinguishes the brother-god installed at Irámuco; given in the Relación in the Spanish orthography Turupten.

purepecha_tiripeme_xungapeti.value: Tarascan; 'Xungápeti' distinguishes the brother-god installed at Pechátaro; given in the Relación in the Spanish orthography Xungapeti / Xugapeti.

topiltzin.evidence: Pinturas1 versus8: distinct narrative contexts, no identity or genealogy transfer.

yucatec_maya_kukulkan.value: Yucatec k'uk'ul 'feathered, quetzal-plumed' + kaan 'serpent', 'Feathered Serpent'; a calque of Nahuatl Quetzalcoatl

nahua_iztac_mixcoatl.evidence: Source-bounded spelling; no indigenous orthographic reconstruction.

nahua_ilancueitl_ancestral.evidence: Source-bounded spelling; no indigenous orthographic reconstruction.
